items.title: PM Anwar hails stronger Q2 expansion, says govt shielded households from global inflation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today welcomed Malaysia’s stronger than expected second quarter growth, saying the 6 per cent expansion underscored the government’s efforts to shield households from global inflationary pressures. In a Facebook post, Anwar described the second quarter growth as the country’s strongest performance outside the pandemic period since 2014, despite global supply disruptions and conflict in West Asia. “This strength was made possible by the Madani government’s efforts to ensure the people’s lives were not severely affected by global inflationary pressures,” he said.

items.title: Two women in dock for allegedly duping retiree in Perak out of RM120,000 over fake tax arrears
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 14 — Two women were charged in the Magistrate’s Court here today with three counts of cheating a male retiree of about RM120,000 by falsely claiming they could help him settle his tax arrears. Noorfarah Surina Ahmad, 42, and Nurfalah Noordin, 33, pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out before Magistrate S. Punitha. The two women allegedly cheated Koay Kuang Hew, 60, by offering to help him settle his tax arrears, which actually did not exist, thereby dishonestly inducing Koay to give them the money, made in three transactions on April 10 and 14 and June 4 this year.

items.title: From FOMO to future jobs: PKR Youth motions put Gen Z outreach in focus
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Youth issues took centre stage at the 2026 National Congress of Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) today, with motions focusing on stronger engagement with Generation Z (Gen Z), jobs of the future, mental health and social wellbeing. Syahnaz Putera Mohd Yaacob, who is Perak AMK Information chief, said PKR faced challenges in winning support from younger voters, particularly Gen Z. “Make mental health and social wellbeing part of the reform agenda.

items.title: Three fight for one spot as vocational college applications surge past 67,000
items.summary: Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the figure was expected to exceed 68,000 when applications close at midnight tonight. He said this reflected strong interest in skills-based education, which was also reflected in the nearly 100 per cent employability rate recorded among KV graduates. He said close collaboration between the MOE and industry players ensured that the fields offered and skills acquired by KV students met job market requirements.

items.title: FGVPI targets RM1bil profit before tax by 2030
items.summary: BANGI: FGV Palm Industries Sdn Bhd (FGVPI) is targeting RM1 billion in profit before tax by 2030, driven by a strategic shift in its business model and improved operational productivity. He said the strategic roadmap includes progressively increasing its profit-before-tax target to RM400 million in 2027, RM600 million in 2028, RM800 million in 2029, and RM1 billion the following year. FGVPI is a subsidiary of FGV Holdings Bhd that operates 63 palm oil mills nationwide, making it one of Malaysia's largest palm oil mill operators, responsible for processing fresh fruit bunches from smallholders and Federal Land Development Authority (FELDA) settler communities.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng rebukes Penang CM Chow, disputes claim DAP delegates endorsed Umno partnership
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Lim Guan Eng has clarified that Penang Pakatan Harapan’s (PH) decision to work with Umno in the state government was not discussed at last week’s Penang DAP delegates’ meeting. Lim said the meeting, attended by current secretary general Loke Siew Fook, focused solely on whether DAP should remain in the federal government, and not on Umno’s role in Penang. “However Chow should not presume that all Penang delegates endorsed his decision merely because no one raised it at Wednesday’s meeting when the Penang DAP delegates were focused on whether to stay or leave the Federal government in Putrajaya,” Lim said.

items.title: Court upholds RM900k payout to businessman over Bentley accident
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today upheld a High Court decision ordering an insurance company to pay a businessman RM900,000 in indemnity for damage to his Bentley Continental GTS V6 MDS in an accident six years ago. A three-member bench led by judge Datuk Dr Choo Kah Sing, sitting with Datuk Ismail Brahim and Datuk Leonard David Shim, unanimously dismissed MSIG Insurance (M) Bhd's appeal against the Kuala Lumpur High Court's decision last year. Choo said it was the defendant's theory that the plaintiff had staged the accident.

items.title: Tonibung renewable energy project wins national award
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: A renewable energy project benefiting more than 20 households and shared community facilities in a remote Ranau village has earned Sabah-based Indigenous-led social enterprise Tonibung a national award. "For Tonibung , a successful renewable energy project is 20 per cent technology and 80 per cent community organising. On Tuesday, Tonibung 's Walou Micro Hydro-Solar Hybrid Project in Kampung Walou, Ranau, was named the winner of Category 3: Renewable Energy - On-Grid (Local) at the National Energy Awards (NEA) 2026 ceremony in Kuala Lumpur.

items.title: Illegal e-waste gets one-way ticket home as Malaysia targets 1,259 containers
items.summary: PORT KLANG, Aug 14 — The Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS) aims to return all 1,259 containers of illegal electronic waste (e-waste) to their countries of origin by year-end. AKPS Port Klang commander Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal said the operation is being conducted in three phases of integrated enforcement, involving about 8,000 metric tonnes of seized e-waste over the past two years in collaboration with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and Port Klang Authority. He said scanning machines at Port Klang remain highly efficient in detecting illegal shipments, but human weaknesses in their operation still pose challenges.

items.title: Eighteen lives lost daily is tough to stomach, but Works Ministry data is finally pointing to the fix
items.summary: KUCHING, Aug 14 — The use of the Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Ministry of Works (KKR) to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur or ‘blackspots’ on federal roads nationwide. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by KKR under the MYJalan initiative, plays a role in systematically managing, analysing and displaying road accident data, including identifying locations where accidents frequently occur. “The average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure,” he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here, today.

items.title: AI boom drives Malaysia's 6pct GDP growth: HSBC senior economist
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's stronger-than-expected growth in the second quarter of 2026 is being powered by the global artificial intelligence (AI) boom, according to HSBC senior Asean economist Yun Liu. Liu said stronger growth reflects Malaysia's deep integration into global electronics supply chains, which has positioned the country to benefit significantly from surging AI-related technology demand. "Despite the energy crisis, Malaysia's Q2 final GDP growth accelerated to 6.0 per cent year-on-year, reflecting the diversity of its economy."

items.title: Teresa Kok denies ignoring Taman Desa security scheme memorandum
items.summary: She said enforcement decisions regarding guarded neighbourhood schemes fall within the jurisdiction of Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and relevant public service agencies. Responding to statements by Taman Desa Phase 1 Residents Association (TDP1RA) president Frank Yeh, Kok said she was neither involved in DBKL's decision-making process nor informed beforehand about an official letter issued by DBKL's urban planning department. She said enforcement actions regarding guarded neighbourhood schemes fall strictly within the jurisdiction of local authorities and public service agencies.

items.title: Bukit Mertajam Hospital makes global green list, ranks among world’s top 250
items.summary: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Aug 14 — Bukit Mertajam Hospital (HBM) here has made history by being ranked among the 250 greenest hospitals in the world in the World’s Greenest Hospitals 2026 ranking by Newsweek and Statista. The Ministry of Health (MOH) said the achievement recognised HBM’s commitment to implementing climate-friendly healthcare practices and environmental sustainability. MOH also congratulated the entire HBM staff and the MOH Engineering Services Division, which were instrumental in the hospital’s sustainability achievement.

items.title: Hop on, KK: BAS.MY pink buses expand eight routes, easing commutes across the city
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Aug 14 — After four months of operation on its initial two routes, Kota Kinabalu’s new fixed-schedule BAS.MY “pink bus” service is now running across all eight routes, giving commuters more options for getting around the city and surrounding areas. The full rollout of routes S01 to S08 began last Tuesday, completing the phased introduction of the service that started on April 1 with routes S01 and S05. The first two routes have already recorded strong demand, with 194,265 passengers using the service between April 1 and August 10.

items.title: ‘Datuk Seri’ businessman claims trial to RM37.1m company funds breach of trust at Bukit Tunku bank
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — A businessman with a “Datuk Seri” title pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to a charge of criminal breach of trust (CBT) involving RM37.1 million in company funds, allegedly committed four years ago. Datuk Seri Zul Azmi Abu Hussin, 51, a director of Xspec Resources Sdn Bhd, was accused of misappropriating RM37,099,999.67 in company funds at a bank in Taman Tunku, Bukit Tunku here on Feb 15, 2022. Deputy public prosecutor Siti Suriatey Mohamed Yusoff applied for bail of RM500,000 with one surety, along with an additional condition that the accused surrender his passport to the court until the case is concluded.

items.title: In-game rewards up for grabs for streamers of MPL MY S18
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mobile Legends: Bang Bang (MLBB) esports fans stand a chance to win a share of 100,000 Diamonds by watching MPL Malaysia Season 18 (MPL MY S18) live on Tonton. The 'Tonton & Menang: MPL MY S18' contest runs from Aug 14 to Nov 1, with 40,000 Diamonds available throughout the Regular Season and another 60,000 Diamonds during the Final Week and Playoffs. Viewers will earn one point for every minute spent watching MPL MY S18 content and matches live on Tonton.

items.title: Road safety: Govt identifies 99 accident blackspots
items.summary: KUCHING:: The Road Accident Management System (RAMS) has enabled the Works Ministry to identify 99 locations where fatal accidents frequently occur, or blackspots, on federal roads nationwide. Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi said RAMS, developed by the ministry under the MYJalan initiative, systematically manages, analyses and displays road accident data, including locations where accidents frequently occur. "An average of almost 18 lives lost every day due to road accidents in Malaysia is a very worrying figure," he told reporters after officiating the closing ceremony of the RAMS Expansion Course and Road Accident Data Reporting here today.

items.title: Generasi Keadilan calls on PKR members to voice people's concerns
items.summary: AYER KEROH: Generasi Keadilan has called on PKR members to remain honest in conveying the people's concerns to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, saying genuine loyalty should also include the courage to speak up when necessary. Its chairman, Yusmadi Yusoff, said support for Anwar and the Madani government should be accompanied by a willingness to raise concerns respectfully and responsibly. Now, we must bring reform to the people," he said.

items.title: Petronas Chemicals' earnings may peak in Q2 FY26
items.summary: This will be supported by stronger petrochemical prices despite lower plant utilisation from planned turnarounds, according to RHB Research. The firm said PetChem's full-quarter benefit from elevated average selling prices (ASPs) should more than offset the temporary impact of lower utilisation. F&M benchmark prices averaged US$680 per tonne for urea, US$728 per tonne for ammonia and US$611 per tonne for methanol.

items.title: Negri MB defends Seremban council's "cash for stray dogs" initiative
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan government wants the public to view the Seremban City Council's (MBS) 'cash for capture' initiative for stray dogs in a positive light, describing it as a proactive move to manage the state's stray population. Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim welcomed MPS' initiative, saying that it is related to public safety. Public safety is our priority.

items.title: Sabah looks to grow Kinabalu Unesco geopark with Tuaran’s natural treasures
items.summary: TUARAN, Aug 14 — The Sabah government is studying a proposal to expand the Kinabalu Unesco Global Geopark (KUGGp) to include parts of Tuaran district, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. Hajiji said KUGGp currently covers an area of about 4,750 square kilometres across three districts, namely Kota Belud, Kota Marudu and parts of Ranau. “In this regard, the Kinabalu Unesco Global Geopark Management Plan 2026-2035 replaces the Interim Management Plan 2021-2025.

items.title: Penang church marks 240 years of Catholic heritage through two world wars
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Church of the Assumption will mark its 240th anniversary tomorrow, having survived two world wars and helped shape Catholic life and education in Penang. Founded in 1786 by French missionary Reverend Father Arnold Garnault with the island's pioneer Eurasian community, the church is Penang's oldest Catholic church and a mother parish from which Catholicism spread across the northern region. The church was initially established on Church Street before the present building along Farquhar Street was constructed in 1860 under Reverend Father Claude Manissol.

items.title: Three months’ jail for man pleading guilty to offensive X posts against Terengganu royalty
items.summary: SEPANG, Aug 14 — A man was sentenced to three months’ jail by the Sessions Court here today after pleading guilty to five charges of making offensive posts against the Terengganu royalty via X. Judge Ahmad Fuad Othman handed down the sentence against Azman Hakim Hassanuddin, 35, and ordered the jail term to run from his remand date of June 24. He stressed that offences touching on the royal institution, religion and racial sensitivities must be taken seriously because they can have a wide impact on society.

items.title: Schools may close if API readings exceed 200
items.summary: TAIPING: Schools in areas where the Air Pollutant Index (API) reading exceeds 200 may be closed at the discretion of the principal or headmaster, based on monitoring and advice from the state Education Department (JPN) and district Education Office (PPD). Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the Education Ministry (MOE) had existing guidelines on managing the effects of haze, including circulars issued in 2016, 2019 and 2023. He said JPN and PPD would monitor haze conditions and API readings from time to time, while school administrators were responsible for making decisions based on local conditions and the advice received.

items.title: Penang exco says traffic fixes before proposed Tanjung Bungah–Batu Ferringhi reclamation project
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — The identification of the coastal area from Tanjung Bungah to Batu Ferringhi as a potential area for reclamation in the Penang State Structure Plan 2040 (Review) (RSNPP 2040) does not mean that the state government has decided to implement the project. State Infrastructure, Transport and Digital Committee chairman Zairil Khir Johari said the area was only identified as a location with potential for future reclamation based on studies including geographical and hydrological aspects. Zairil said the same thing happened when the Middle Bank area was identified as a potential area for reclamation in the previous structure plan, but it was not implemented.

items.title: Bukit Aman say they know how Malaysia Airlines pilot cleared KLIA checks after three-day interrogation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Police are pursuing members of a drug syndicate in Malaysia after a Malaysia Airlines pilot was arrested in Jakarta late last month with more than 26 kilogrammes of drugs in his luggage. According to Berita Harian (BH), Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the operation followed intelligence obtained after investigators interrogated the pilot over two days. Hussein said the investigation also allowed NCID to share key intelligence on international drug syndicates with relevant agencies.

items.title: Jobless single dad claims trial to robbing and injuring mum with baby at Batu Gajah house
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 14 — An unemployed man pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to a charge of robbing and causing injury to a woman last week. Lee Koon Yew, 49, was charged with committing the offence against Fatin Fazira Ahmad Fauzi, 26, at a house in Taman Batu Gajah Perdana at 11.40 am on Aug 8. Earlier, Deputy Public Prosecutor M. Raveena proposed bail of RM20,000 with one surety.

items.title: Penang MMEA detains Indonesian vessel over alleged illegal fishing
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) detained an Indonesian fishing vessel yesterday for allegedly encroaching into Malaysian waters and fishing without permission. The unregistered wooden vessel was detected by the Penang MMEA during a routine patrol by KM Semilang. Penang Maritime director Maritime Captain Muhammad Suffi Mohd Ramli said the vessel was intercepted at 11.20am, about 38 nautical miles southwest of Pulau Kendi.

items.title: Married couple plead guilty to causing death of three-month-old baby under their care in Johor
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 14 — A husband and wife were charged in the Sessions Court here today with causing the death of a three-month-old baby boy who was under their care in Masai last month. The accused, Mohd Iqbal Hassan, 36, and his wife, Norsiayana Abd Samad, 34, pleaded guilty after the charge was read to them before Judge Datuk Che Wan Zaidi Che Wan Ibrahim. According to the charge sheet, the couple, as persons having custody of Muhammad Saif Mohamad Sidiq, exposed the baby in a manner likely to cause him physical injury, resulting in his death.

items.title: Nurul Izzah’s PKR leave has no end date yet, says party sec-gen
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) has not set a timeframe for deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar’s leave from party duties as she plans to pursue further studies. PKR secretary-general Senator Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said the party was prepared to welcome Nurul Izzah back to her duties when she was ready to resume her responsibilities. “The deputy president will go on leave after the party’s National Congress.

items.title: Not just train stops: ECRL stations are getting a Malaysian glow-up, telling East Coast stories
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 14 — Every major East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) station is an architectural tribute to its state’s heritage, history, and culture, transforming each stop into a living showcase of local identity, not just a transit point. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said this approach ensures ECRL development highlights the cultural and heritage uniqueness of communities along its route. Loke said in Pahang the KotaSAS Station design is inspired by the state crest, featuring the ‘Gading Gajah’ (elephant tusk), while the Gombak Integrated Terminal Station draws inspiration from the Gombak Selangor Quartz Ridge, a 14-kilometre-long quartz formation.

items.title: PKR members leaving for Bersama have little impact on party - Youth chief
items.summary: AYER KEROH: The departure of some PKR members to join Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) has had minimal impact on the party and has not disrupted its organisation, said PKR Youth chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. He confirmed that some members had applied to leave PKR after losing confidence in the party and choosing to join Bersama, which has been taken over by former PKR deputy president Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli. "Yes, I do not deny that there have been applications by party members to leave the party.

items.title: ECRL Kota Bharu–Gombak service targets December 2026 launch, a month ahead of schedule
items.summary: GOMBAK, Aug 14 — The East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) Phase 1 service from Kota Bharu to Gombak is targeted to commence operations as early as December, earlier than the original schedule in January 2027. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the target depends on the smoothness of the ongoing testing and commissioning processes, including the System Integration Testing (SIT) and Fault-Free Run (FFR), without any compromise on safety aspects. “We are trying to see how the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) can help facilitate matters related to the testing and certification processes to expedite this project without compromising safety.

items.title: 1,259 e-waste containers targeted for shipment by year-end
items.summary: KLANG: The Port Klang Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) is targeting the shipment of 1,259 containers of electronic waste (e-waste) out of Malaysia by the end of this year through a joint operation involving various agencies. Its commander, Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal, said 148 containers had been sent out under the first phase of the operation. He said that under the ongoing second phase, the agency, in collaboration with the Port Klang Authority and the Customs Department, had shipped out 255 of the 533 containers.

items.title: US flags Malaysia in China tariff-evasion crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: US trade regulators have flagged Malaysia among more than 40 trade partners identified as risks for aiding tariff evasion, as Washington intensifies its global crackdown on China-linked transshipment networks. Citing five government and private-sector economic models, the report estimates total annual illegal transshipment trade flows between US$40 billion (Goldman Sachs estimate) and US$303 billion (Altana estimate), with the Council of Economic Advisers using a US$60 billion midpoint baseline. A US Commerce Department transaction-level analysis revealed that transshipment alone drains an estimated US$28 billion annually in uncollected customs revenue from the US Treasury while undercutting American industrial output.

items.title: Indonesia to close more than 750 state-owned enterprises
items.summary: JAKARTA: Indonesia's president mulled the possibility of a special court on Friday to investigate "unproductive" boards reporting "made up" profits, as he vowed to close 750 state-owned enterprises by year end. "There are far too many unproductive state-owned enterprises, always reporting losses while claiming profits – those profits are just made up," Prabowo said in his state of the nation address to parliament. With the establishment last year of Indonesia's Danantara sovereign wealth fund to manage state assets, "we discovered that there are 1,074 state-owned enterprises," the president told lawmakers.

items.title: 82,092 candidates offered undergraduate spots in 20 public universities
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A total of 82,092 candidates have been offered bachelor's degree placements at 20 public universities this year, according to the Higher Education Ministry (MoHE). In a statement today, MoHE announced that the figure represents 76.10 per cent of the 107,875 applications eligible to pursue undergraduate studies via UPUOnline. Overall, a total of 1,146 bachelor's degree programmes are offered for this session.

items.title: A way out after 23 years? Govt offers Semantan Estate settlement in Duta Enclave dispute
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — After more than two decades of legal battles over 106 hectares of prime Kuala Lumpur land now occupied by major federal institutions, the government has offered Semantan Estate (1952) Sdn Bhd a settlement to resolve its compensation claim. The offer was disclosed at the High Court here today, where both parties informed Justice Roslan Mat Nor that Putrajaya had extended the settlement proposal, although its terms and value were not disclosed, news outlet Free Malaysia Today reported. Semantan Estate applied to postpone today’s hearing to give the company time to consider the offer, but Roslan rejected the application and ordered the hearing to proceed as scheduled.

items.title: Law student fined RM500 for allowing account to be used in illegal transactions
items.summary: Judge Madihah Zainol ordered Nicole Soo Lik Yee to serve one month in jail if she fails to pay the fine. Soo was charged with dishonestly transferring RM525 belonging to a 32-year-old man into her bank account at Jalan Idaman 8/10, Taman Nusa Idaman, Iskandar Puteri, at 4.31pm on June 13. Deputy public prosecutor Shamira Mohd Luthfi Ismail prosecuted.

items.title: High chance of haze persisting until late September
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hazy conditions are expected to persist until late September, although the situation nationwide remains under control for now, says the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia). Its director-general, Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip, said current haze levels have not reached the extremes seen in previous episodes, except in Sarawak. Dry weather since late July has heightened the haze risk in Sarawak, compounded by transboundary smoke from West Kalimantan, Indonesia.

items.title: Farage wins UK by-election as Count Binface claims 'moral victory'
items.summary: CLACTON-ON-SEA, United Kingdom: Hard-right British politician Nigel Farage reclaimed his seat in a by-election, according to the final tally Friday, though his main rival and joke candidate Count Binface took an larger than expected share of the ballot. Farage, who triggered the vote by resigning the parliamentary seat he had held since 2024 over an investigation into his finances, swept 63 per cent of the ballots in the English constituency of Clacton. While votes were still being counted, Farage had declared victory.

items.title: Toyo Tyre puts Malaysia at heart of growth push
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Toyo Tyre is putting its Malaysian manufacturing operations at the centre of its growth strategy, combining local production capabilities with Japanese engineering as it seeks to strengthen its position in an increasingly competitive tyre market. The Japanese tyre maker recently unveiled its new brand manifesto, "Buatan Malaysia, Keunggulan Jepun", positioning Malaysian manufacturing and Japanese technology as key differentiators while seeking to make premium-quality tyres more accessible to local motorists. Toyo Tyre Malaysia president and managing director Mike Toh said its Taiping plant is advancing its intelligent manufacturing transformation (IMX) programme to create a smarter, more efficient and sustainable manufacturing ecosystem.

items.title: Thai schools tighten security after deadly shooting
items.summary: BANGKOK: Students stood quietly outside their Bangkok school Friday as teachers checked their bags, pockets and even pencil cases under new security measures introduced after last week's deadly shooting. "An incident like this should not have happened in a school," headteacher Suparong Sawangngamwong told AFP after overseeing the new checks at Bangkok's Sawasdee Wittaya School. A modest public school nestled among the city's affluent neighbourhoods, Sawasdee Wittaya has more than 500 pupils aged six to 12, and 30 teachers.

items.title: KLIA Transit offers 50pc return fare discount to Putrajaya, Cyberjaya for National Day
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Express Rail Link Sdn Bhd (ERL) is offering a 50 per cent discount on KLIA Transit return tickets to Putrajaya and Cyberjaya in conjunction with Malaysia’s 69th National Day celebrations. In a press statement today, ERL said the promotion covers journeys from KL Sentral, Bandar Tasik Selatan and Salak Tinggi between August 29 and 31. Children aged five and below can travel free with every adult ticket purchased, subject to a maximum of three children per adult.

items.title: Higher-quality investments may take time to lift wages, household incomes: Bank Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's efforts to attract higher-quality investments and move up the value chain could eventually translate into higher wages and household incomes, although the benefits may take time to filter through the economy. Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said stronger economic growth did not immediately translate into higher household incomes as there was usually a time lag before the benefits reached the population. Abdul Rasheed said the country needed to continue attracting quality investments, moving up the value chain and improving productivity to support higher wages and incomes.

items.title: Bank Negara approves RM2.8bil financing under SME relief facility
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bank Negara Malaysia has approved about RM2.8 billion in financing under its SME Stabilisation Relief Facility (SME SRF), benefiting more than 4,900 small and medium-sized enterprise (SME) accounts affected by the Middle East conflict. Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said the facility was introduced to provide working capital support to viable businesses, including microentrepreneurs, to sustain operations amid economic disruptions arising from the conflict. Abdul Rasheed said financing conditions for SMEs also remained healthy, with outstanding SME financing growing 4.2 per cent in the second quarter of 2026.

items.title: KJ says new Tabung Haji RCI premature
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former Umno Youth chief Khairy Jamaluddin says it is premature to establish a new Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) into Tabung Haji. He said a detailed management report or audit should first determine why the fund's asset recovery plan had fallen short. Speaking on the latest episode of the Keluar Sekejap podcast, Khairy said the underperformance of assets transferred to Urusharta Jamaah Sdn Bhd (UJSB) did not, by itself, justify another RCI, as it remained unclear whether the assets were unrecoverable or the recovery plan had failed.

items.title: Pulau Jerejak as financial hub? Putrajaya backs plan to boost Penang’s high-tech sector
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Pulau Jerejak has the potential to be developed as a financial hub to complement the semiconductor and high-tech sector in Bayan Lepas. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said based on a briefing from developer Ideal Property, about 32.37 hectares on Pulau Jerejak are slated for an integrated development. On a related note, he said a new bridge connecting Pulau Jerejak to the Penang mainland is expected to support the island’s development.

items.title: Stop dwelling on losses, focus on way forward, says Fadhlina
items.summary: PKR Wanita chief Fadhlina Sidek said after the conclusion of the PKR congress on Sunday, the wing must go down to the ground, activate initiatives and engage with women. "We must knock on every door. We must organise now.

items.title: Police identify drug syndicate links in Malaysian pilot's case
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian narcotics investigators have obtained crucial information how the Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested with drugs in Jakarta managed to clear security checks at the Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA). Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said investigators had also uncovered information on the local and international drug syndicates linked to the case, including individuals believed to be part of their networks. He said the pilot had also cooperated well with Malaysian investigators during the questioning sessions.

items.title: Malaysia could become high-income nation by 2029 as tech drives exports, says deputy minister
items.summary: Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said Malaysia is currently classified as an upper middle-income country, and recent economic developments, including the country’s trade performance, indicate that it is moving in a positive direction. He said the country’s export structure has also undergone a significant transformation, with electrical and electronic (E&E) products – including semiconductors – accounting for 42.5 per cent of exports, while machinery and equipment contributed 12.6 per cent. “We’re slowly moving towards becoming a technological country, with E&E, machines, and high-tech products accounting for more than half of our total exports.

items.title: Two face conspiracy charges over alleged healing scam
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Two women arrested recently over an alleged traditional healing scam were charged in the Sessions Court here today with three counts of criminal conspiracy to cheat three women. Malaysian Hee Nyin Fung, 48, and Chinese national Li Li, 38, pleaded not guilty to two charges before judge Zaini Fishir @ Fisal and another before judge Monica Linsua after the charges were read to them in Mandarin. On the first charge, Hee, a businesswoman, and Li, a company director, allegedly conspired to cheat a 51-year-old woman at the Kota Kinabalu Central Market at 7.30am on Feb 4.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng hits back at Chow over Penang PH-Umno cooperation
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: DAP adviser Lim Guan Eng has hit back at Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman Chow Kon Yeow over the coalition's decision to work with Umno. Lim said Chow appeared to be confused when he claimed that no objection had been raised to Penang PH's decision to accept Umno's role in the state government during a DAP Penang delegates' gathering on Wednesday. "Chow must be confused when he said that at the Penang DAP's delegates gathering attended by DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke on Wednesday night, neither I nor anyone raised any objection to Penang PH's decision to work and accept Umno's role in the Penang state government," he said in a statement.

items.title: ‘Being popular alone is not enough’: Youth chief tells PKR leaders to rebuild grassroots strength
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 14 — Parti Keadilan Rakyat (PKR) needs to put forward a more compelling narrative to strengthen people’s confidence in the party, said Angkatan Muda Keadilan (AMK) chief Muhammad Kamil Abdul Munim. He said grassroots strength must also be further strengthened and translated into victories in the next election. The congress, which was opened by PKR deputy president Nurul Izzah Anwar, was also attended by PKR vice-president Datuk Seri Dr Zaliha Mustafa and Wanita PKR chief Fadhlina Sidek.

items.title: Sim Tze Tzin dismisses PKR turmoil talk, says core leadership united under Anwar
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — PKR strategy director Sim Tze Tzin today dismissed claims of internal turmoil in the party, saying its core leadership remains united under president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Sim said the party’s upcoming national convention would provide delegates with a platform to raise concerns following electoral setbacks in Johor and Negeri Sembilan, while allowing leaders to identify and address weaknesses before the next general election. The core leaders remain steadfast in the party,” he said.

items.title: MetMalaysia: Sarawak’s hot, dry spell could keep haze hanging around till Aug 20 while thunderstorms lash peninsula
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Hot and relatively dry weather is expected to persist in Sarawak and several other areas of Borneo until Aug 20, potentially increasing the risk of haze and reducing visibility, particularly in southern Sarawak. As of 10am today, 10 areas nationwide recorded Air Pollutant Index readings at unhealthy levels, based on data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System portal, with the majority of the locations in Sarawak. The warning also covers several areas in Perak, namely Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Manjung and Bagan Datuk, as well as Selangor, including Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Klang, Petaling, Gombak and Hulu Selangor.

items.title: Chow Kon Yeow says Penang DAP takes no stance, leaves Cabinet exit motion to delegates
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 14 — Penang DAP has not adopted an official position on a motion calling for the party to leave the Cabinet, instead leaving the decision to its delegates at the DAP Convention on Sunday. DAP central executive committee member Chow Kon Yeow said Penang delegates had been briefed on the motions to be debated and voted on at the convention. He said Penang DAP did not take an official state position.

items.title: Teo Nie Ching insists Johor DAP won’t dictate, delegates hold Cabinet fate in Sunday congress
items.summary: KULAI, Aug 14 — Johor DAP delegates are free to decide whether the party’s leaders should remain in government posts, including the federal Cabinet, or relinquish those positions while continuing to support Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, ahead of the special congress this Sunday. Johor DAP chief Teo Nie Ching said the state leadership is leaving it to more than 400 delegates, who have the freedom to make decisions based on their respective views and understanding of the party’s direction. We give the freedom to the delegates or representatives to make that decision at DAP’s national congress this Sunday.

items.title: Malaysia’s inflation outlook steady at 1.5–2.5 pc, BNM stresses external pressures remain manageable
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia’s headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent in the second quarter of 2026 from 1.6 per cent in the preceding quarter, while core inflation moderated to 1.9 per cent from 2.1 per cent, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said today. BNM Governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said higher input costs had so far seen limited pass through to consumer prices. The central bank’s figures showed producer cost pressures were concentrated at the upstream stage, with crude materials prices rising 27.5 per cent and intermediate inputs 3.7 per cent, while finished goods prices increased 1.4 per cent.

items.title: One year after son attacked, Rafizi decries threats, says case ‘died off’ unresolved
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 14 — After a year since the attack on his child in Putrajaya, Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli has claimed the case has “gone quiet and died off”. “A year has passed, and the case has gone quiet,” he wrote on Facebook, adding that he had been informally told by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail of a suspected mastermind, but his request for an open statement in Parliament was rejected. Rafizi vowed to continue seeking justice.
